goal: A highly polished, responsive browser-based decision board styled as a private strategy atelier. It allows small teams to input options, score them from 1 to 5 across customizable criteria, view a deterministic leader, and persist data locally. The interface features a warm parchment background, charcoal ink typography, restrained brass accents, and subtle tactile depth, completely avoiding generic SaaS dashboard tropes.
constraints: Must use exactly five files: index.html, styles.css, app.js, journey.json, README.md
No external dependencies, CDNs, or network requests
Must adhere strictly to the parchment, charcoal, and brass visual palette
Must be fully keyboard-navigable and responsive
Exclusion or preservation: No external CDNs, libraries, or frameworks (e.g., Tailwind, React, FontAwesome)
Exclusion or preservation: No network calls or external API dependencies
Exclusion or preservation: No neon gradients, glassmorphism, or oversized modern metric cards

Approved visual direction: Private strategy atelier aesthetic: warm parchment background (#FDFBF7), deep charcoal ink text (#1C1A17), muted brass accents (#A38A5E), elegant serif headers (Playfair Display or Georgia), clean sans-serif body text, subtle borders resembling fine stationery, and smooth, deliberate micro-interactions.
Operating context: Modern desktop and mobile browsers (Chromium, Safari, Firefox)
Operating context: Fully responsive layout adapting from mobile screens to wide desktop monitors
acceptance_criteria: Users can add, edit, and delete decision options
Users can score options from 1 to 5 across at least three default criteria
The highest-scoring option is dynamically highlighted as the leader
Board state persists across page reloads using LocalStorage
A 'Clear Board' button requires explicit confirmation before wiping data
The UI matches the strategy atelier aesthetic with high typographic contrast and tactile borders
Successful execution of a multi-step Chromium journey verifying option creation, scoring, and leader calculation
Zero console errors or warnings during standard operations
Visual verification of the parchment-and-brass editorial theme
Explicit confirmation dialogs before any destructive state changes
